# Sources and acknowledgements

<!-- GENERATED by pipeline/scripts/generateAttributions.ts — do not hand-edit.
     Regenerate after changing any manifest. -->

This engine's understanding of Scripture is not its own. Every theme it
recognises and every term it treats as evidence comes from people who spent
their lives explaining the Bible, and from communities who catalogued it. This
page names them.

**What ships and what does not.** The commentaries and expositions below are
read only at BUILD time. Their prose never enters the published artifact and is
never read at query time. What ships is a distillate: a term, a score, a count,
and a pointer back to who attested it. That distinction is deliberate, and it
is why sources whose *transcriptions* carry restrictions can still inform the
statistics without their text being redistributed.

**Attribution is a requirement here, not a courtesy.** OpenBible.info's data is
CC BY 4.0, which requires attribution in shipped output. This file is where
that obligation is met.

---

## Expositors

The verse-level evidence layer. A term is admitted only when **two or more of
these authors, independently, used it about the same verse** — which is what
separates the passage's theology from any one writer's habits of speech.

**The bound on that independence, stated plainly:** every expositor below is
Protestant, writing between the early 18th and the early 20th century (Matthew
Henry's commentary appeared 1706-1721; Maclaren's *Expositions* in the 1900s).
Corroboration establishes independence of *authorship* — Spurgeon cannot
corroborate Spurgeon — but not independence of *interpretive tradition*:
authors who share a school of reading will agree for reasons the corroboration
rule cannot see. There is real internal spread here (Clarke is Wesleyan, Spurgeon
Reformed Baptist, Delitzsch Lutheran, and the set mixes philological commentary
with preaching), but it is spread *within* anglophone-dominated Protestant
exposition of that period. The engine reports the evidence as what it is — what
these expositors reached for — rather than as a neutral property of the text.
The concept layer, where provenance is per-anchor and editorial judgment is
labeled as editorial, is where a different or broader voice **could** enter
deliberately; today its own sources (Torrey, OpenBible votes, LH editorial) sit
inside the same broad tradition.

## Declared for lineage only

These are not imported. They are recorded so that sources deriving from them
can declare that lineage, which keeps the engine from counting the same
scholarship twice as independent evidence.

- **LH editorial** — Authored for this dataset. LH holds all rights. Drafted with AI assistance offline and admitted by human review; no AI runs at query time.
- **LH editorial (public-domain hymn index)** — Authored for this dataset (QR-6, 2026-08-22). LH holds all rights to the alias rows themselves. Every hymn indexed in the starter pack is verifiably public domain in the United States (pre-1930 publication; per-row provenance in ontology/aliases/hymn-lines.yaml). Titles and short first-line phrases are not copyrightable (US Copyright Office Circular 33), and no hymn lyrics beyond a title or a first-line/refrain phrase are stored. Hymnary.org's index is not openly licensed and was not used (J38).
- **Nave's Topical Bible** — Public domain by age (Orville J. Nave, Topical Bible, 1897; Nave died 1917). Not directly imported; declared so that sources deriving from it can express that lineage for correlation budgeting (G7).
- **Cross-translation vocabulary (KJV, ESV, NIV, NLT)** — DERIVED INDEX ONLY. No translation text is stored or shipped. What this source contributes is, per verse, the set of word STEMS appearing in some English translation of that verse but not in the shipped one — unordered, deduplicated, stopwords removed, stemmed, and merged across all four sources so no single translation's contribution is separable. There is no word order, no punctuation and no function words, so the prose cannot be reconstructed from it. KJV is public domain (eBible.org verse-per-line export). ESV, NIV and NLT are copyrighted; licensed copies held by Jesse Freeman were read ONCE, locally, to derive this index, and never entered this repository or the artifact. The relationship is that of a search index to the works it indexes rather than a copy of them. Recorded here in full because the distinction is the entire basis on which this source is admitted, and a reader must be able to check it rather than take it on trust.
- **Treasury of Scripture Knowledge** — Public domain by age (published 1830s). Not directly imported; declared so that sources deriving from it can express that lineage for correlation budgeting (G7).

## What is deliberately absent

- **Modern sermon libraries.** Several offer their material free of charge —
  Life.Church Open among them — but free of charge is not the same as licensed
  for redistribution. Life.Church's terms grant use "for your internal use and
  not for resale" and forbid exercising the granted rights "toward commercial
  advantage", which does not permit a publicly distributed artifact. Recorded
  here so the question does not have to be re-asked.
- **Copyrighted translations.** NIV, ESV and similar cannot be included. This
  has a visible consequence: a verse remembered in NIV wording may not match
  the public-domain text the engine searches.
- **CCEL's own transcription files**, where an alternative source exists. Where
  one does not, see the rights note on the affected source above.
